4BfRDZLIiznSnwU7DdDL9N: The story goes that Dave McCabe of the Zutons wrote this in a taxi, in about twenty minutes, on the way to his mum's. A song to a friend in America who'd got herself in trouble over her driving. I have some sympathy. I put a whole ferry on a sandbank and nobody wrote me a song. [dryly] Plenty of letters, mind. Mark Ronson says Amy Winehouse hardly listened to anything made after nineteen sixty-seven, and you can hear it: she sings it like it was always hers. Valerie, Mark Ronson with Amy Winehouse. Wait for the horns.
40b31eggZB30hoqXhGm4qc: Two of the band quit just before they went to Lagos to make this album, and then the three who were left got robbed at knifepoint, demo tapes and all. So Paul McCartney, Linda and Denny Laine made the songs again from memory. I like that. Half of what I play out here I could play from memory too, because the label's gone or there's sand in the groove. The orchestra came later, back in London, and it's the moment the whole thing opens up. A song about getting out, for a man who's only ever halfway out. Band On The Run, Paul McCartney and Wings.
2aoo2jlRnM3A0NyLQqMN2f: [quietly] Noel Redding walked out halfway through recording this. He liked the Bob Dylan version better. So Dave Mason from Traffic was on twelve-string, Brian Jones from the Stones shook the rattle you hear at the start, and the bass, so the engineer says, he played himself. Then he spent months in New York laying guitar over guitar, because he kept hearing it a little bit differently. I know the feeling. I've rewired the transmitter four times and it still isn't how I hear it in my head. All Along the Watchtower, by Jimi Hendrix, and every one of those overdubs earned its place.
3u2s7Dppp5ID2MxKnqxFyh: Bruce Springsteen wrote this with a rhyming dictionary, because his record company said his first album didn't have a single on it. There's bits of his own life in there, his drummer's nickname, his old Little League team. His version didn't do much. Then this lot put a bit of Chopsticks in the middle and took it to number one in America, and that's still Springsteen's only number one as a songwriter. Somebody else's band, his song. I drove the van for a band once. Nobody ever covered them. Blinded by the Light, Manfred Mann's Earth Band, all seven minutes, which is how I like it.
29capylmokCeuNAWqGitij: In the old Indian films the actors don't really sing. They mouth along, and a playback singer does the singing out of sight. Asha Bhosle sang thousands of them, and this is a thank you to her, and to the little forty-five singles. First time out it got to number sixty. Then Norman Cook sped it up, pushed the key up, and it went all the way to number one. I like both. The singer you never see doing the real work... [dryly] a man on a boat nobody's supposed to find has some sympathy for that. Brimful of Asha by Cornershop, the Norman Cook mix.
7o7E1nrHWncYY7PY94gCiX: Trevor Horn says he got this from a J. G. Ballard short story, and from hearing Kraftwerk and feeling that something new was coming and something old was on its way out. He put in Radio Luxembourg too, the station he listened to as a boy. Funny thing is, Bruce Woolley, who wrote it with them, put out his own version first, and plenty of people say his is the better one. I'm not taking sides. I'm just glad the radio part didn't die. Out here the radio star is a man in a jumper with a gull on his aerial. Video Killed The Radio Star, The Buggles.
3yrSvpt2l1xhsV9Em88Pul: It was meant to be called Brown Skinned Girl. Van Morrison says the word changed while they were recording, by mistake, and he only noticed when he saw what was written on the tape box. Twenty-two takes in a New York studio, a contract he signed without a lawyer, and he says he's never had a penny from it. He also says it's not one of his best, that he's got about three hundred better. [sighs] I'd argue with him, but I bought a trawler without reading much of the paperwork either, so I'm in no position. Van Morrison, Brown Eyed Girl.
3zBhihYUHBmGd2bcQIobrF: Otis Redding started this on a rented houseboat in Sausalito, when he wanted to change his style a bit. He finished it in Memphis with Steve Cropper, and he still thought of it as not quite done. After Otis was gone, Cropper mixed it and put the waves and the gulls on, because Otis had asked for them. So those gulls are there on purpose. I told Gerrit. He took it as a compliment and has been impossible ever since. What gets me is how little he does with that voice here, and how much it says. Otis Redding, Sittin' On the Dock of the Bay.
4c6vZqYHFur11FbWATIJ9P: Lee Mavers wrote this, and then spent nearly three years in studios with one producer after another, chasing a sound in his head that none of them could catch. When the album finally came out, the band turned their backs on it. People have argued for years that it's about heroin. Mavers says flatly that it isn't, and I'll take a man's word about his own song. What I hear is somebody running after a girl he can't quite keep up with. [quietly] Someone I knew used to play it twice, every time. Never once. Anyway. The La's, There She Goes.
2AX5E86cn9n2dgioZEjirI: The record company hated this one. You can't dance to it, they told the band, you're finished. It went to number two. Hugh Cornwell says the words work two ways, a girl and heroin, and when the bass player told the papers about the second one, some of the radio stations dropped it. Cornwell reckons that cost them number one. On this boat the only drug is coffee and the playlist is whatever comes out of the keeper's crate. [dryly] We'd have kept playing it. Golden Brown, the Stranglers.
4BP3uh0hFLFRb5cjsgLqDh: John Fogerty says he wrote this in about twenty minutes, sitting on the edge of his bed, angry. Angry about the war and his own draft notice, and about the sons of senators and the like who never seemed to end up anywhere near it. Since then everybody's tried to borrow it, jeans adverts, politicians, and he's objected to most of them. Good for him. I hear a man with something to say and no time for decoration. When I walked out of the warehouse I didn't take twenty minutes either. Creedence Clearwater Revival, and Fortunate Son.
2Vim06YsRb4uJRpbeq6NR6: Joe South wrote this for Billy Joe Royal, leaning on the dashboard of a car on the way to Nashville, because Royal didn't like the other song South had going. A song that had to go round the world to get anywhere. The keeper's crate is full of records like that. I've always had a soft spot for them. Hush, Deep Purple.
05oETzWbd4SI33qK2gbJfR: Stevie Nicks wrote this before she'd even joined the band, after reading a novel called Triad with a woman named Rhiannon in it. Only years later did she find out Rhiannon was a goddess from old Welsh stories, and after that she'd introduce it on stage as a song about an old Welsh witch. I like that the song knew more than she did when she wrote it. Some of the bottles that wash up against the hull are like that. A listener writes two lines and I read five things into them. Probably wrong about all five. Rhiannon, Fleetwood Mac.
390AWnOn2rfe9FzQjYmxIH: [warmly] This one owes everything to a man in my line of work. It came out and almost nobody noticed. One stubborn bloke with a microphone. I think about him more than I should. That guitar is James Calvin Wilsey, leaning on the whammy bar. The song's about wanting someone who isn't good for you, and it doesn't pretend to have an answer. Wicked Game, Chris Isaak.
0UAJH0k4k3slcE83a9UGCe: Ray Davies says this is based on something that really happened to him, but not every word. Somebody asked him to dance in a club, he said no, and she went off in a taxi with his manager. That's one version. There are others, and the drummer has his own. What I love is the guitar: a Dobro from nineteen thirty-eight and an acoustic together, squeezed hard, so it rings like a tin roof. It was number one in the Netherlands, and I once heard a whole ferry deck sing the chorus, crew and all, with the captain pretending not to. The Kinks, Lola.
5QTxFnGygVM4jFQiBovmRo: Buck Dharma wrote this thinking about what would happen if he died young. People heard a suicide pact in it, and that appalled him. Listen to how gentle that guitar line is; it's not a song that wants anybody to go anywhere. When Opa stops dead I always think, well, that's it then, and he always coughs and starts again. [dryly] So far. Blue Öyster Cult, Don't Fear the Reaper. They had to cut the solo down, and I'd have left it long.
5e9TFTbltYBg2xThimr0rU: This started out as a Christine McVie song called Keep Me There, and hardly any of it survived. Bits of everything, and it holds. Fleetwood Mac, The Chain.
5fztgDIt1Nq32VHJrAHq0Y: Joni Mitchell went to Hawaii for the first time, woke up in her hotel, looked out and saw a parking lot where she wanted paradise. That's where this comes from. 5YUJMvTg4AWHKjqQidTsGK: Pete Shelley was in a guest house in Edinburgh, a few pints in, half watching Guys and Dolls on the telly, when somebody in the film said a line about falling for someone you shouldn't. 5EWPGh7jbTNO2wakv8LjUI: For two years Ronnie Van Zant told Allen Collins he had too many chords to sing over. I carried a band's gear once. Nobody asked me to join. Lynyrd Skynyrd, Free Bird.
